prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1351; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind at a stop. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the photographs taken at the scene. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's account of how the collision occurred.

Entry 3: Witness statements were obtained and both independently describe the impact as it is recorded in the file. Their accounts are consistent with the scene photos.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage to the rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp assembly is consistent with the reported force of the impact. No prior damage to these areas appears in our records or in the inspection notes.

Entry 5: Claimant reports neck and back strain. The described injury is a typical result of a collision of this type and force, and no prior injury to the same body area is known to us.

Entry 6: Police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver is listed on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Claimant's account of events has stayed the same in every recorded conversation, including the initial call, the recorded statement and later correspondence through counsel.

Entry 8: Medical treatment began with an initial evaluation and physical therapy. Over the following months, visit frequency increased and additional services were added, which is more than is usually needed for this injury. Requested records from the treating providers.

Entry 9: Reviewed the treatment billing against typical care for a strain of this kind. The extended course and added services are noted for discussion with the medical reviewer before any settlement position is set.

Entry 10: Referred the treatment question to the medical review unit and sent the attorney a request for updated records and a current treatment plan. Next review scheduled once the response is received.
